meetings.headline: Finance Committee questioned the treasurer on low investment yields and gave input on the FY25 capital plan ranking.
meetings.summary: The committee reviewed the town's year-end cash report and municipal investments with the treasurer. Members pressed for higher returns, and she explained the legal limits on how municipal funds may be invested. They then discussed capital planning input for FY25, including school project shifts, MSBA uncertainty, and whether Parks should be prioritized separately from facilities. The budget season calendar and future meetings were reviewed, and the meeting adjourned.

meetings.headline: Finance Committee split 2-2 on supporting the school's modified Primary School cooling plan; vote is advisory and fails.
meetings.summary: The committee heard the school department's request for support of a modified plan using ductless mini-split units at the Primary School in place of the original air conditioning project. Members debated process, scope, and lifespan, and the support motion failed on a tie; the chair noted the vote is advisory and the town manager decides. The committee also appointed members to the master plan steering committee and capital planning committee, set a summer schedule, and approved prior minutes.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee split 2-2 on whether to support the school department's modified Primary School cooling plan, so the support motion failed.
The chair noted the committee is advisory and cannot stop or force the project; the town manager, Select Board and School Committee are to weigh the result.
The motion was amended to use the amount town meeting appropriated, because the school's letter cited a different figure.
The modified plan uses ductless mini-split units in place of the original air conditioning project, whose engineer estimates ran far higher.
The committee appointed one member to the master plan steering committee and another to the capital planning committee, and set a summer meeting schedule.

why_it_matters: The Primary School cooling project may come back as a larger capital request needing a debt exclusion, which residents would be asked to vote on and which would draw on the town's limited debt capacity.
The tie leaves the Finance Committee without a recommendation, so the decision rests with officials who are not bound by its vote.
